headlines.title: Booking Holdings (BKNG) Stock Could Be A Bargain Despite AI Spending
headlines.summary: Booking Holdings has seen its share price decline in recent months, which puts fresh focus on whether today's US$154.46 level is adequately supported by the cash the business is expected to generate. With new artificial intelligence initiatives rolling out across its brands, the key issue is how those projects intersect with the stock's cash flow profile. Over the past 5 years, Booking Holdings has delivered a total return of 68.

headlines.title: What Could Booking Holdings (BKNG) AI Travel Push Mean For Its Stock?
headlines.summary: Booking Holdings (NasdaqGS:BKNG) has launched Vayo, an AI travel agent that books complete trips across its own and rival platforms. Vayo can coordinate flights, hotels, car rentals and other trip components in one flow, comparing options from multiple online travel services. KAYAK, a Booking Holdings brand, has rolled out 28 new AI-driven planning tools that mix conversational search with live pricing.

headlines.title: Why Booking Holdings (BKNG) Is Getting Attention Today
headlines.summary: Booking Holdings (BKNG) has pushed further into AI-driven trip planning after expanding Vayo, its personal travel agent. It now books flights, stays, transport, activities and more within a single conversation for private beta users. For investors, the backdrop is more mixed than the product news suggests. Booking Holdings’ share price has slipped over the shorter term, with a 1-day move down 1.95% and a 90-day share price return down 27.

headlines.title: Booking Holdings' Vayo Now Books the Entire Trip
headlines.summary: Vayo, the personal travel agent from Booking Holdings (NASDAQ: BKNG), today announced that it can now book every part of a traveler's trip. Just one month after its debut, Vayo enables travelers to discover, compare and book flights, hotels, rental cars, restaurants, activities and more across online travel platforms and directly with suppliers, all within a single conversation. headlines.title: Booking Holdings vs. GameStop: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
headlines.summary: Booking earns a high-margin travel business with strong free cash flow, while GameStop is mid-pivot toward capital allocation. The valuation gap between them is narrower than the business models suggest.

description: Booking Holdings Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides online and traditional travel and restaurant reservations and related services in the United States, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and internationally. The company operates Booking.com, which offers online accommodation reservations; and Priceline, which provides discount travel reservations services, as well as online accommodation, flight, rental car reservation services, vacation packages, cruises, activity, and affiliate programs. It also operates Agoda that offers online accommodation reservation, flight, ground transportation, and attractions. In addition, the company operates KAYAK, an online meta-search service that allows consumers to search and compare travel itineraries and prices; and OpenTable for booking online restaurant reservations, as well as reservation management services to restaurants. Further, it offers travel-related insurance products, payment facilitation, and restaurant management services to consumers, travel service providers, and restaurants; and advertising services. The company was formerly known as The Priceline Group Inc. and changed its name to Booking Holdings Inc. in February 2018. Booking Holdings Inc. was founded in 1997 and is headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut.
